newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn can't halve unemployment by 2000 - DIW.
newsitem.headline: Bonn can't halve unemployment by 2000 - DIW.

text.p: The head of German economic research institute DIW said on Thursday Bonn's goal of halving unemployment by the year 2000 was unrealistic and that a cut to 3.4 million was the best that could be achieved in the time.

The government has repeatedly stated its goal is to halve joblessness but those statements were made when unemployment totalled about four million people. The latest figures show a surge by more than 500,000 people in January to 4.66 million.
Lutz Hoffmann, president of Deutsches Institut fuer Wirtschaftsforschung, said past experience showed the German economy could create at most 250,000 additional jobs per year.
"That would amount to about 750,000 and would take the jobless total down to 3.4 million," Hoffmann said in a radio interview.
Asked to comment on the government's goal, Hoffmann said, "We don't regard that as very realistic."
Hoffmann also warned against attempts to cut real wages and said this would pose big problems for German industry. Many German firms have been complaining about continued weak domestic demand.
Germany needed moderate wage gains which did not exceed productivity gains, Hoffmann said.
"One cannot say we lack competitiveness," Hoffmann said. Germany was not at a disadvantage to neighbouring countries in terms of unit labour costs.
German Chancellor Helmut Kohl drew criticism from unions on Wednesday for calling on Germans to accept little or no real wage increases over the next few years in a bid to create jobs.
